description: split_equally drops cents on uneven totals

issue.title: split_equally drops cents when the total doesn't divide evenly
issue.body:
`split_equally` is documented to assign every cent (leftover cents go one each to the first people, so the shares add up to `total_cents`), but it just floor-divides and discards the remainder:

```python
>>> split_equally(100, ["ann", "bob", "cy"])
{'ann': 33, 'bob': 33, 'cy': 33}   # sums to 99, one cent has vanished
```

`balances()` is built on it, so the loss shows up there too. The net balances for one shared expense should always sum to zero, but:

```python
>>> balances([Expense("ann", 100, ("ann", "bob", "cy"))])
{'ann': 67, 'bob': -33, 'cy': -33}   # sums to 1
```

**Expected**

- `split_equally(100, ["ann", "bob", "cy"])` returns `{"ann": 34, "bob": 33, "cy": 33}`.
- The shares always sum to `total_cents`, for any total and group size.
- Net balances from `balances()` sum to zero.

Please add tests for the uneven cases.
